intro.text: 今天的主线不是又一个更大的模型，而是模型怎样真正进入工作流：Vercel 在补齐 agent 的持久化底座，Trajectory 在把生产数据变成持续学习的闭环，Garry Tan 则用实测提醒大家，模型选择要看单位任务成本，而不是排行榜。更有意思的是，Builder 们开始把「经验」本身当成下一层基础设施：谁能把真实任务、反馈和 reward 接起来，谁才更接近可用的 AI 产品。

archive.title: 持续学习日报
archive.desc: Agent 正从一次性调用走向可持久、可评估、能从真实任务经验中持续变好的系统。

sections.title: The Loop Is the Product / 闭环本身就是产品
sections.desc: 真正的 continual learning 不只是训练一个模型，而是把生产轨迹、评估、训练和部署接成一条能反复运行的产品链。

rewrite: The takeaway: continual learning becomes useful when training, eval, and deployment live in one loop. Trajectory founder Ronak describes today's agents as closer to offline maps: smart, but forced into batch updates whenever the route changes. The target is Google Maps for AI, where every real-world task becomes a new trace and the system keeps improving.

The practical bottleneck is not just model architecture. Teams need production traces, replayable environments, and a way to turn 'what good looks like' into reward. Trajectory packages that path into a one-click train-and-deploy workflow; in the Harvey example, a specialized model moved from roughly 4% to 18% accuracy while costing six times less than a frontier model.
original: And I think by doing this of of basically putting training, eval, and deployment in one place, making that just dead simple for every single person to do, And then you can close the loop and basically now upload that model back to production, gather new traces.
With Trajectory, what they were able to do is train a model that is six times cheaper, and it goes from around 4% accuracy for an open source model to around 18%.

rewrite: 核心结论是：continual learning 只有在训练、eval 和部署处于同一个闭环里时，才真正有用。Trajectory 创始人 Ronak 说，现在的 agent 更像离线地图：能力很强，但路线一变就得整批更新。理想状态是 AI 版 Google Maps，每次真实任务都变成新的 trace，系统持续变好。
实际瓶颈不只是模型架构。团队还需要生产环境里的 trace、可回放的环境，以及把「什么叫好」转成 reward 的方法。Trajectory 把这条链路包装成一键训练和部署；在 Harvey 的案例里，专用模型准确率从约 4% 提升到约 18%，成本却只有 frontier model 的六分之一。
original: 把 training、eval 和 deployment 放在一起，让每个人都能简单使用，然后把模型上传回生产环境，收集新的 traces，形成闭环。
用 Trajectory 训练出的模型便宜六倍，准确率从开源模型的大约 4% 提升到大约 18%。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch says Workflow SDK 5 and Vercel Workflows are a major step for agents because the hard parts are becoming infrastructure, not bespoke application code. First-step latency and the gaps between steps improved, encryption and security got more attention, and the system has been exercised against large-scale reliability and disaster-recovery scenarios.
The most important detail is the reusable durability log: Vercel is turning the machinery that makes a workflow survive interruptions into a durable harness that other agent systems can use.
original: Workflow SDK 5 and Vercel Workflows are a monumental step forward for agents.
We made the underlying durability log reusable for any agent harness. durable-harness was born.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 认为，Workflow SDK 5 和 Vercel Workflows 对 agent 的意义在于：最难的部分正在变成基础设施，而不是每个应用都要自己重写的代码。首步延迟和步骤间等待都改善了，系统也强化了加密、安全、规模化可靠性和灾难恢复。
最关键的细节是可复用的 durability log：Vercel 把让 workflow 在中断后继续工作的那套机制，抽成任何 agent harness 都能使用的 durable harness。
original: Workflow SDK 5 和 Vercel Workflows 是 agent 的一大步。
我们让底层 durability log 可以被任何 agent harness 复用，durable-harness 诞生了。

sections.title: Measure the Work, Not the Hype / 衡量任务，不要迷信榜单
sections.desc: 当模型能力接近时，真正影响工程选择的是 solved task 的成本、可靠性和对具体 workflow 的适配。

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan's recommendation is unusually concrete: keep Opus 5.5 as the Claude Code default. In a 52-task comparison, Fable 5.2 solved nearly the same share of coding tasks, 82.7% versus 84.6%, but cost 2.8 times more per solved task.

That is a useful reminder for builders: once a model already clears most ordinary tasks, the relevant benchmark is no longer the headline score. It is the cost of getting a real task over the line, especially on the harder cases.
original: Keep Opus 5.5 as your coding default in Claude Code. On 52 coding tasks in Claude Code 2.1.322, Fable 5.2 solved about as many (82.7% vs 84.6%) but cost 2.80x as much per solved task.

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan 给出的建议非常具体：Claude Code 里继续把 Opus 5.5 作为默认模型。在 52 个 coding task 的对比中，Fable 5.2 的解决率几乎一样，82.7% 对 84.6%，但每个 solved task 的成本高了 2.8 倍。
这提醒 builder：当一个模型已经能解决大多数普通任务时，真正该看的就不再是 headline score，而是让真实任务成功落地的成本，尤其是难题上的成本。
original: Claude Code 里把 Opus 5.5 作为 coding 默认模型。52 个 coding task 的测试中，Fable 5.2 解决率差不多（82.7% 对 84.6%），但每个 solved task 的成本高 2.80 倍。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari pushes back on benchmark-maxxing: there is no substitute for running models on your own workflows. Only a few benchmarks actually matter, and the rest can become marketing hill-climbing that says more about the test than the product.
The editorial point is simple: an eval should answer whether the system works for the job you need, not whether it can win a leaderboard built around somebody else's job.
original: There’s no substitute to really using the models for your workflows to understand the best ones that actually work for your workflows.
In reality, there’s only very very few benchmarks that truly matter, and the real ones know.

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari 反对 benchmark-maxxing：没有什么能替代把模型放进自己的 workflow 里跑。真正重要的 benchmark 很少，剩下的很容易变成围绕测试集爬榜，最后证明的只是测试本身，而不是产品。
判断标准其实很简单：eval 应该回答系统是否适合你要做的工作，而不是它能不能赢下一张围绕别人工作方式设计的排行榜。
original: 没有什么能替代真正把模型用于自己的 workflow，去理解哪些模型对你的 workflow 真正有效。
现实是，真正重要的 benchmark 非常少，真正懂的人知道是哪几个。

sections.title: Agents Need Experience / Agent 需要经验
sections.desc: 今天最值得注意的方向，是把真实世界里积累的经验接回模型，而不是只把模型当成一次性的智能 API。

rewrite: Peter Yang shares a concrete example of turning an agent into a research assistant for long-term illness: put a patient's medical records in a folder, give ChatGPT or Claude the /fuck-cancer skill, and ask it to produce a one-page brief or research clinical trials. He also invites people to fork the skill for other conditions.

The important signal is not the provocative name. It is the workflow: domain documents become context, a reusable skill becomes the procedure, and the output is a focused brief rather than a generic chat.
original: Upload all of the patient's medical records (e.g., to a Google Drive folder)
Tell ChatGPT or Claude to install my free /fuck-cancer skill ... to create a one-page brief, research clinical trials, and more.

rewrite: Peter Yang 分享了一个把 agent 变成长期疾病研究助手的具体 workflow：把患者病历放进文件夹，让 ChatGPT 或 Claude 使用 /fuck-cancer skill，再让它生成一页 briefing 或查找临床试验，也可以 fork 这个 skill 用到其他疾病。
真正值得注意的不是这个有挑衅意味的名字，而是它的结构：领域文档提供上下文，可复用的 skill 提供流程，最后输出的是一份聚焦的 brief，而不是泛泛聊天。
original: 把患者所有医疗记录上传到文件夹（比如 Google Drive）。
让 ChatGPT 或 Claude 安装免费的 /fuck-cancer skill，用来生成一页 brief、研究临床试验等。

rewrite: Dan Shipper asks why teams still pay for software even when Fable 5.2 can 'vibe code anything.' The implied answer is that software value is not just the code: it includes the workflow, reliability, context, and the accumulated experience that makes the result useful in an organization.
That is the missing bridge between impressive demos and durable products. Agents can generate more interfaces, but the moat moves toward owning the process and the data around the work.
original: why teams still pay for software even when Fable 5.2 can vibe code anything:

rewrite: Dan Shipper 提了一个很好的问题：即使 Fable 5.2 能「vibe code anything」，团队为什么还愿意为软件付费？暗含的答案是，软件价值不只是代码，还包括 workflow、可靠性、上下文，以及让结果在组织里真正可用的积累经验。
这正是 demo 和耐用产品之间缺的那座桥。Agent 能生成更多界面，但护城河会转向你是否拥有工作流程，以及围绕这些工作沉淀下来的数据。
original: 即使 Fable 5.2 能 vibe code anything，为什么团队还在为软件付费？

sections.title: Commerce and the Durable App / Agent 走进真实业务
sections.desc: Agent 的下一步不只是会写代码，而是进入支付、企业应用和具体业务流程，接受真实的规模与约束。

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad says the company has been working with Visa on agentic commerce, with more features and use cases to come. It is a short product update, but it points at the real test for agents: can they participate in transactions and business workflows, not just generate a prototype?
original: It's been great partnering with @Visa on agentic commerce. More features and use cases are coming!

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 表示，公司正在和 Visa 合作推进 agentic commerce，后续还会有更多功能和场景。这是一条很短的产品更新，但它指向了 agent 的真实考场：它能不能参与交易和业务流程，而不只是生成一个 prototype？
original: 很高兴和 Visa 合作推进 agentic commerce，更多功能和场景即将到来。

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch's terse prediction, 'Vercel Sandbox is inevitable,' lands beside the Workflow update as a clear infrastructure thesis: agents need isolated, repeatable environments where they can safely execute work. The sandbox is not a side feature when the agent is expected to run code, recover from failure, and operate over time.
original: Vercel Sandbox is inevitable

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch 那句「Vercel Sandbox is inevitable」，和 Workflow 的更新放在一起看，是一个很清晰的基础设施判断：agent 需要隔离、可复现的环境，才能安全执行任务。只要 agent 要运行代码、从失败中恢复并长期工作，sandbox 就不再是边角功能。
original: Vercel Sandbox 是不可避免的。
